newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rabo sees modest Dutch inflation, no overheating.
newsitem.headline: Rabo sees modest Dutch inflation, no overheating.

text.p: Inflation in the Netherlands will rise modestly this year and in 1998, but the economy is not overheating, Dutch cooperative bank Rabobank said on Wednesday.
Rabobank said in a research note it expected inflation to rise from 2.1 percent in 1996 to 2.25 percent in 1997 and 2.50 percent in 1998.
"The Dutch economy is currently operating at a high pace. A more detailed approach, however, makes clear that there is as yet no real shortage of production factors," the bank said.
"In general capacity seems sufficient to take care of increasing demand so that demand-driven inflation pressures are quite limited."
Healthy Dutch economic growth, coupled with falling unemployment, low interest rates and surging share and house prices have led to concern about lurking inflation dangers.

But Rabobank said that, while inflation could blip up to around three percent in the summer due to exceptional factors like the current swine fever outbreak in the country, there was little danger of runaway price increases in the longer term.
"The Dutch economic engine seems under control," the bank said. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
